nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis Ni3Fe-CO3 LDH
nodes.procedure: Ni3Fe-CO3^2- LDHs with different sizes and thicknesses were synthesized by regulating the hydrothermal temperature (Fig. S1, ESI†). TEM and atomic force microscope (AFM) images visually demonstrate that for Ni3Fe-CO3^2- LDHs, both lateral size and layer number will be decreased by low hydrothermal temperature (Fig. S2 and S3, ESI†), especially Ni3Fe-CO3^2- LDH-60°C.
nodes.source_text: Ni3Fe-CO3^2- LDHs with different sizes and thicknesses were synthesized by regulating the hydrothermal temperature (Fig. S1, ESI†)... especially for Ni3Fe-CO3^2- LDH-60°C.

unit_operations.name: Hydrothermal reaction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: synthesized by regulating the hydrothermal temperature

nodes.name: Anion Exchange
nodes.procedure: During the anion exchange step, interlayer CO3^2- is exchanged by PtCl6^2- to acquire the SAC precursor (Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH). CO3^2- can be entirely replaced by PtCl6^2- in interlamination.
nodes.source_text: During the anion exchange step, interlayer CO3^2- is exchanged by PtCl6^2- to acquire the SAC precursor (Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH)... CO3^2- can be entirely replaced by PtCl6^2- in interlamination and thus synthesizing Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH with atomic dispersion of Pt.

unit_operations.name: Anion Exchange
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: interlayer CO3^2- is exchanged by PtCl6^2- to acquire the SAC precursor

nodes.name: Space-confined Electroreduction
nodes.procedure: By the electrochemical reduction process of removing Cl ligand from PtCl6^2-, Pt single-atom is anchored in interlamination, and CO3^2- enters interlamination because of electrostatic adsorption from the alkaline electrolyte. After the first LSV curve (50 mV s^-1) for the electrochemical reduction of Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH, HER activity remains stable, which indicates that electroreduction can remove Cl ligand from the interlayer PtCl6^2- and anchor Pt single-atom swiftly in Ni3Fe LDH. During the SACs synthesis process from Ni3Fe-CO3^2- LDH to Ni3Fe-CO3^2- LDH-Pt SA, the morphology and crystal structure remained unchanged without aggregation of Pt atoms, besides, in EDS analysis, sharply declining Cl atom ratio indicated that the electrochemical reduction could remove Cl ligand of PtCl6^2- to anchor Pt single-atoms.
nodes.source_text: By the electrochemical reduction process of removing Cl ligand from PtCl6^2-... For Ni3Fe-CO3^2- LDH-Pt SA, the interlayer CO3^2- anions come from the CO3^2- anions in alkaline electrolyte.

nodes.source_text: Ni₃Fe-CO₃²⁻ LDH-Pt SA has outstanding HER performance, reaching 10 mA cm⁻² with an overpotential of 45 mV... Tafel slope value of Ni₃Fe-CO₃²⁻ LDH-Pt SA is 37.8 mV dec⁻¹... HER performance barely decays during 12 hours... mass activity of Ni₃Fe-CO₃²⁻ LDH-Pt SA is 2.5 times greater than that of 20 wt% Pt/C
results in excellent OER performance 218 mV overpotential to reach 10 mA cm⁻²... Fig. S33 shows the good stability for OER performance
using Ni₃Fe-CO₃²⁻ LDH-Pt SA as both the anode and cathode for overall water splitting, it can achieve 10 mA cm⁻² at a low cell voltage of 1.50 V
even better than 20 wt% Pt/C (51 mV)

nodes.description: HER mechanism analysis via operando EIS
nodes.source_text: results in mixture mechanisms (Heyrovsky–Volmer and Tafel–Volmer) rather than Heyrovsky–Volmer mechanism

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show diffraction peaks at 11.4° (003) and 23.0° (006) representing 7.7 Å interlayer spacing for CO₃²⁻ anion, and 8.4° (003) and 16.6° (006) representing 10.5 Å for PtCl₆²⁻ anion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In XRD patterns of LDHs, the diffraction peaks of 11.4° (003) and 23.0° (006) represent 7.7 Å for the interlayer spacing of CO₃²⁻ anion; the diffraction peaks of 8.4° (003) and 16.6° (006) represent 10.5 Å for the interlayer spacing of PtCl₆²⁻ anion.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR spectra show absorption band at 1354 cm⁻¹ for symmetric stretching vibration of interlayer CO₃²⁻, which vanishes after anion exchange with PtCl₆²⁻ and reappears after electroreduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption band around 1354 cm⁻¹ in FTIR spectra, represents the interlayer CO₃²⁻ (7.7 Å) and symmetric stretching vibration of interlayer CO₃²⁻, respectively, completely vanishes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra identify PtCl₆²⁻ with absorption bands at 173.5, 319.5, and 350.5 cm⁻¹, which appear after anion exchange and vanish after electroreduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The precise variations of CO₃²⁻ and PtCl₆²⁻ anions were identified from Raman and FTIR spectra, respectively... three absorption bands of PtCl₆²⁻ at 173.5, 319.5, and 350.5 cm⁻¹ in Raman spectra appeared.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images show highly dispersed Pt single-atoms anchored in Ni₃Fe LDH nanosheets with intact layered structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the HAADF/ABF-STEM images focusing on the front and the side-face of Ni₃Fe–CO₃²⁻ LDH-Pt SA nanosheets, highly dispersed Pt single-atoms were seen to be anchored in the Ni₃Fe LDH nanosheet after electroreduction.

properties.features: nanostructured material with lattice fringes, crystalline nanoparticles

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with ordered stripe-like or layered morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Pt 4f shows Pt valence state decreased from Pt⁴⁺ (73.1 eV) to Ptᵟ⁺ (71.3 eV); area ratio of Pt 4f to Cl 2p much higher after electroreduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS shows that, at Pt 4f, Pt valence state decreased from Pt⁴⁺ (73.1 eV) to Ptᵟ⁺ (71.3 eV) with increasing cycles of electroreduction... The area ratio of Pt 4f to Cl 2p in Ni₃Fe–CO₃²⁻ LDH-Pt SA is much higher than that of Ni₃Fe-PtCl₆²⁻ LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES at Pt L3-edge shows white-line intensity of Ni3Fe–CO3^2- LDH-Pt SA lower than Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH but higher than Pt foil, confirming Pt^δ+ single-atom.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The white-line intensity of Ni3Fe–CO3^2- LDH-Pt SA is significantly lower than that of Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH, but higher than that of Pt foil, suggesting that Pt^δ+ single-atom with a positive charge has been anchored.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS Pt L3-edge FT k^3χ(k)-R space shows Pt-Cl at ~1.90 Å for Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH and Pt-O at ~1.66 Å for Ni3Fe–CO3^2- LDH-Pt SA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FT k^3χ(k)–R space curves... show the Pt–Cl contribution (peak around 1.90 Å) for Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH and Pt–O contribution (peak around 1.66 Å) for Ni3Fe–CO3^2- LDH-Pt SA.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows mass fractions of Ni (23.4 wt%), Fe (6.9 wt%), and Pt (9.7 wt%) in Ni₃Fe-PtCl₆²⁻ LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) shows mass fractions of Ni (23.4 wt%), Fe (6.9 wt%) and Pt (9.7 wt%) in Ni₃Fe-PtCl₆²⁻ LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER shows Ni²⁺/Fe³⁺-OH vibrations at 448 and 526 cm⁻¹ before 1.415 V, transforming to Ni²⁺ᵟ-O-Fe³⁺ᶻ vibrations at 468 and 546 cm⁻¹ after electrooxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through in situ Raman for Ni₃Fe–CO₃²⁻ LDH-Pt SA during OER, before 1.415 V, the weaker peak (448 cm⁻¹) and stronger peak (526 cm⁻¹) represent vibrations of Ni²⁺/Fe³⁺-OH in Ni₃Fe–CO₃²⁻ LDH-Pt SA; after electrocatalyst electrooxidation potential (1.415 V), the stronger peak (468 cm⁻¹) and weaker peak (546 cm⁻¹) appear.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XAS during OER shows Ni valence state increases at electrooxidation potential (1.40-1.45 V), slows during OER (1.45-1.55 V); Fe valence increases slightly after 1.40 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on in situ XAFS spectra for Ni₃Fe–CO₃²⁻ LDH-Pt SA during OER, Ni valence state increases obviously at the electrooxidation potential (1.40 to 1.45 V); during drastic OER (1.45 to 1.55 V), the increase of Ni valence state slows down; Fe valence state increases slightly after 1.40 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES Ni K-edge and Fe K-edge show Ni-O bond length unchanged but Fe-O bond length shortened in Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH compared to Ni3Fe–CO3^2- LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni–O bond length appears to be identical between Ni3Fe–CO3^2- LDH and Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH... compared with Ni3Fe–CO3^2- LDH, the Fe–O bond length of Ni3Fe-PtCl6^2- LDH was obviously shortened.
